mainTopic: The חלה measure derived from the עומר of מן, then a new משנה on a חצר and a מרפסת without an ערוב, and the debate between רב and שמואל over a spot reached by lowering versus throwing
overview: This amud opens by finishing a discussion about food measurements. The גמרא asks how much dough is obligated in חלה. The answer is 'like your dough', which means like the dough of the desert: the daily עומר of מן, a tenth of an איפה. From this the חכמים set the חלה amount at seven רבעים of flour plus a little, the same amount as six Jerusalem quarters or five ציפורי quarters. They also say that eating about this much each day is healthy. Then a new משנה begins. When the people of a חצר and the people of a מרפסת above it did not make an ערוב, any raised spot in the חצר that is ten טפחים high and within four טפחים of the מרפסת belongs to the מרפסת, and anything else belongs to the חצר. The גמרא first lists obvious cases, sorted by how each side reaches a spot: through an entrance, by throwing, or by lowering. It then asks about a spot that one side reaches by lowering and the other by throwing. רב says both sides are forbidden to use it. שמואל says the side that lowers gets it, because easy use beats hard use. The גמרא begins testing this debate against our משנה, and the argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How much is 'your dough'?
steps.stepSummary: The text states that the חלה measure is 'like your dough' (from the פסוק of ראשית עריסותיכם), then asks how much that actually is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The measure is the amount of 'your dough.' And how much is 'your dough'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of discussing food measurements. It quotes the rule that dough is obligated in חלה when it is 'the size of your dough,' then asks what that size is. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says to give חלה from 'your dough' (עריסותיכם) but never gives a number. So the question is how to turn a vague word into an actual measurement.

keyTerms.meaning: your doughs (from the פסוק about חלה)
the amount of / as much as
and how much?
the portion of dough given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a discussion. The topic of חלה came up because the גמרא was measuring how much food makes a meal, which matters for the size of an ערוב.

phrases.english: The amount of 'your dough,'
phrases.notes: Based on the פסוק 'ראשית עריסותיכם' (במדבר טו).

phrases.english: And how much is 'your dough'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of food measures on the previous amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual size of 'your dough', the amount that obligates חלה.

steps.title: Your dough equals the dough of the desert
steps.stepSummary: 'Your dough' means the amount of food eaten in the desert, the מן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the amount of the dough of the wilderness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'your dough' is measured by the 'dough of the desert,' meaning the daily portion of מן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the normal daily portion the Jews ate in the desert sets the standard for 'your dough.' This only moves the question one step back, since we still need the size of the desert portion.

keyTerms.meaning: the dough of the desert, meaning the daily portion of מן

phrases.english: As the amount of the dough of the wilderness.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חלה measure equals the daily portion of מן in the desert.

steps.title: How much was the dough of the desert?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the actual size of the desert portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is the dough of the wilderness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question: how big was the desert portion? This sets up the פסוק that gives a real number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 linked one unknown to another unknown. Now the גמרא needs a source with an actual measurement.

phrases.english: And how much is the dough of the wilderness?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question on the answer of step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The numerical size of the daily מן portion.

steps.title: The עומר is a tenth of an איפה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the עומר (the daily מן portion per person) is one tenth of an איפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the עומר is a tenth of the איפה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק that gives the size of the עומר: one tenth of an איפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person collected one עומר of מן a day (שמות טז:טז). פסוק לו says an עומר is a tenth of an איפה. An איפה is 3 סאין, which is 18 קבין, 72 לוגין, or 432 ביצים, so an עומר is 43.2 ביצים.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is written
the daily portion of מן per person
a large dry measure: 3 סאין
a tenth

steps.whyThisMatters: This פסוק is the numerical source for the שיעור of חלה used in halacha.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And the omer is the tenth part of the eifa.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The desert portion is an עומר, which is one tenth of an איפה.

steps.title: Seven quarters of flour and a bit more are obligated in חלה
steps.stepSummary: From the עומר calculation, the חכמים set the חלה measure at seven רבעים of flour plus a little. They also gave its value in Jerusalem and ציפורי measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: seven quarters (of a קב) of flour and a bit more are obligated in חלה. That equals six by the Jerusalem measure, which equals five by the ציפורי measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the practical rule: dough made from seven רבעים of flour plus a little more must have חלה taken. It then converts the amount into two larger local systems of measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עומר is 43.2 ביצים. A רובע (quarter קב) is 6 ביצים, so seven רבעים are 42 ביצים, and the 'ועוד' covers the extra 1.2. Each later system was a fifth larger than the one before it. This is the same as adding a sixth, counted from the new, larger total. So a Jerusalem quarter is 7.2 ביצים, and the עומר is exactly six of them. A ציפורי quarter is about 8.64 ביצים, and the עומר is exactly five of them.

keyTerms.meaning: from here they said, a rule drawn from the source
quarters of a קב
and a little more
the Jerusalem measure (larger)
the ציפורי measure (even larger)

steps.whatToRemember: The שיעור of חלה is one עומר: seven רבעים of flour and a bit more. This equals 6 Jerusalem quarters or 5 ציפורי quarters, since all three are the same amount in different measuring systems.
steps.confusionAlert: Seven, six, and five are not three different amounts. They are the same amount of flour measured with bigger and bigger units.

phrases.english: From here they said,
seven quarters (of a kav) of flour and a bit more
is obligated in challah,
which are six of the Jerusalem measure,
which are five of the Tzippori measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ שִׁבְעָה רְבָעִים קֶמַח וָעוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the פסוק of step 4 into a practical halachic measure.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Dough of seven רבעים of flour plus a little (one עומר) is obligated in חלה.

steps.title: Eating this amount daily is healthy
steps.stepSummary: From the same עומר measure, the חכמים say that eating about this much a day is healthy and blessed. More is gluttony, and less shows a stomach problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: one who eats this amount is healthy and blessed. More than this is a glutton. Less than this has damaged bowels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a second lesson from the עומר: it is the healthy daily amount of food for a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מן was given as one עומר per person per day, so that amount is treated as the natural, balanced portion. Eating more is excess, and eating less points to a digestive problem. This ties back to why the topic came up: the measure of normal meals, which matters for the size of an ערוב.

keyTerms.meaning: healthy and blessed
a glutton
has damaged bowels, an unhealthy stomach
more than this

steps.whatToRemember: The עומר is both the שיעור of חלה and the model of a healthy daily food portion.

phrases.english: From here they said:
One who eats like this measure
is healthy and blessed.
More than this is a glutton.
Less than this has damaged bowels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel lesson drawn from the same עומר measure as step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: About one עומר of food a day is the healthy amount. More is excess, and less signals illness.

steps.title: New משנה: courtyard and balcony residents who forgot to make an ערוב
steps.stepSummary: When the people of a חצר and the people of a מרפסת above it forgot to make an ערוב together, an object in the חצר that is ten טפחים high belongs to the מרפסת. Anything lower belongs to the חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Residents of a courtyard and residents of a balcony who forgot and did not make an ערוב: anything ten handbreadths high belongs to the balcony. Anything less than that belongs to the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with two groups sharing space, a ground-level חצר and a raised מרפסת, who did not make an ערוב with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without an ערוב, each group may only use its own area on שבת. A mound or post in the חצר that is ten טפחים tall counts as its own רשות, closer in use to the מרפסת, so the מרפסת people get to use it. If it is lower, it is basically part of the ground, so it belongs to the חצר.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the text of the משנה begins
a shared courtyard
a balcony or raised walkway that the upper apartments open onto
made an ערוב, joining their areas for carrying on שבת
ten handbreadths, the standard height that makes a separate domain

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new משנה within the same פרק, not the start of a new פרק. The ten-טפחים rule decides which group may use the raised object, not whether carrying is allowed at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the following גמרא, which will explore which uses count and how the ten-טפחים line divides shared spaces.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Residents of a courtyard and residents of a balcony
who forgot and did not make an eiruv,
anything that is ten handbreadths high belongs to the balcony.
Less than this belongs to the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַנְשֵׁי חָצֵר וְאַנְשֵׁי מִרְפֶּסֶת שֶׁשָּׁכְחוּ וְלֹא עֵירְבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the measurement discussion before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without an ערוב, an object in the חצר that is ten טפחים high belongs to the מרפסת, and anything lower belongs to the חצר.

steps.title: The same rule for a cistern rim and a rock
steps.stepSummary: The ten-טפחים rule from the previous step also applies to the raised rim around a בור and to a rock.
steps.simpleTranslation: The raised rim of a cistern, and a rock: if they are ten handbreadths high, they belong to the balcony. If they are lower than that, they belong to the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same ten-טפחים rule to two more objects: the raised rim around a בור and a rock standing in the חצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the rule itself. The point is that the rule covers any raised surface, not just a mound. If it is ten טפחים tall it is easy to reach from the מרפסת, so it belongs to the people up there. If it is lower, it is part of the ground level and belongs to the חצר.

keyTerms.meaning: The raised rim or embankment built around a cistern
A rock
Ten handbreadths, the standard height that counts as a separate area

phrases.english: The embankment of a cistern, and the rock,
if they are ten handbreadths high,
they belong to the balcony;
less than this, they belong to the courtyard.
phrases.notes: Same split as step 7, applied to new objects.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ten-טפחים rule of step 7 to more objects.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cistern rim or rock ten טפחים high goes to the מרפסת; anything lower goes to the חצר.

steps.title: The rule only works when the object is near the balcony
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits the ten-טפחים rule. It applies only when the object is near the מרפסת. A distant object goes to the חצר even if it is tall.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this rule said? When the object is near the balcony. But if it is far away, even if it is ten handbreadths high, it belongs to the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a condition: being tall is not enough. The object must also be close to the מרפסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason a tall object goes to the מרפסת is that its people can reach it easily. If the object is far from the balcony, they cannot reach it easily anymore. So the people of the חצר, who can walk right up to it, get it.

keyTerms.meaning: "In what case is this said?" A formula that limits an earlier rule
Near, close by
Distant, set apart

steps.confusionAlert: Height alone does not decide the case. A tall object that is far from the balcony still belongs to the חצר.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
When it is near the balcony.
But when it is distant,
even if it is ten handbreadths high,
it belongs to the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ten-טפחים rule to objects that are near the balcony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tall object goes to the מרפסת only if it is near; if it is distant, it goes to the חצר.

steps.title: Defining "near" as within four handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines "near": anything less than four טפחים away from the מרפסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what counts as near? Anything that is not four handbreadths away.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives an exact measurement for the word "near" that it just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה asks the question itself and answers it right away, so this is a definition, not a real debate. Less than four טפחים from the balcony counts as near. Four טפחים or more counts as distant, and the object goes to the חצר.

keyTerms.meaning: "And which is it?" A formula that introduces a definition
Four handbreadths, a standard minimum size or distance

steps.whatToRemember: An object goes to the מרפסת only if two things are true: it is ten טפחים high, and it is less than four טפחים from the balcony. Otherwise it goes to the חצר.

phrases.english: And what is considered near?
Anything that is not four handbreadths away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an exact measure for the word סמוכה used in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Near means less than four טפחים from the מרפסת.

steps.title: Obvious case: both sides reach it easily, like a window
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by saying it is obvious that a place both sides can reach easily follows the law of a window between two חצירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It is obvious. If one side reaches it through an entrance and the other side reaches it through an entrance, this is the same as a window between two courtyards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by listing cases whose answer is obvious. This sets up a harder question that will come later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both sides can reach a place with equal ease, neither side has a stronger claim. So it has the same law as a window between two חצירות. That law is already known: without a shared ערוב, the two sides restrict each other from using it. The word פשיטא tells us the real question will be about a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is obvious." Marks a case that is clear, usually before a harder question
An entrance; here it means easy, direct access
A window between two courtyards, a known case of equal access
"This is the same as"

phrases.english: Gemara:
It is obvious:
if it is for this side through an entrance and for that side through an entrance,
phrases.notes: Both sides have easy, direct access.

phrases.english: this is the same as a window between two courtyards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins its analysis by sorting out the obvious cases of equal access.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both sides have easy access, the place follows the law of a window between two חצירות.

steps.title: More obvious cases: like a wall, or like a ditch
steps.stepSummary: Two more obvious cases. If both sides can reach the place only by throwing, it is like a wall. If both can reach it only by lowering, it is like a ditch.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one side reaches it only by throwing and the other side only by throwing, this is the same as a wall between two courtyards. If one side reaches it only by lowering and the other side only by lowering, this is the same as a ditch between two courtyards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list of obvious cases. In each one here, both sides have the same kind of access. The list goes on in the next step before the real question is asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both sides can reach the place only by throwing things up onto it, it matches the known law of a wall between two חצירות. If both can reach it only by lowering things down into it, it matches the law of a ditch. Equal access means an equal claim. The next step shows that the cases where one side walks in through an opening are also already decided. The real question, in step 14, is when one side lowers and the other throws.

keyTerms.meaning: Throwing; reaching a place only by tossing things onto it
Lowering; reaching a place only by letting things down into it
A wall
A ditch or trench

steps.whatToRemember: All three obvious cases have equal access on both sides, so each one simply follows a law we already know: a window, a wall, or a ditch. The real question will be about cases where the two sides have different kinds of access.

phrases.english: If it is for this side by throwing and for that side by throwing,
this is the same as a wall between two courtyards.
If it is for this side by lowering and for that side by lowering,
this is the same as a ditch between two courtyards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of obvious equal-access cases from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throwing on both sides follows the law of a wall; lowering on both sides follows the law of a ditch.

steps.title: Mixed cases where one side has easy access
steps.stepSummary: If one side reaches the place through an opening and the other only by throwing or lowering, these cases were already decided by רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Easy for one side by an opening, but by throwing for the other: this is the ruling רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of רב נחמן. Easy for one side by an opening, but by lowering for the other: this is the ruling רב שיזבי said in the name of רב נחמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list of cases that are already clear. Here one side has easy access and the other side does not, and an earlier ruling of רב נחמן already covers both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases one side walks in easily through an opening and the other side has to struggle. רב נחמן's rulings, reported by two students, give the place to the side with the easy access. So these cases need no new discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: An opening or entrance. The place is reached easily, at ground level.
Throwing. The place is high, so you must toss things up onto it.
Lowering. The place is low, so you must let things down into it.
"This is exactly". This case is already covered by a known ruling.

phrases.english: For this one by an entrance, and for that one by throwing:
phrases.notes: One side walks in; the other must toss things up.

phrases.english: this is the case of Rabba bar Rav Huna,
who said in the name of Rav Nachman.
phrases.notes: The place goes to the side with easy access.

phrases.english: For this one by an entrance, and for that one by lowering:
this is the case of Rav Sheizvi,
who said in the name of Rav Nachman.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of obvious cases from steps 11-12, now with mixed access.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one side has easy access through an opening, the place goes to that side, as רב נחמן ruled.

steps.title: The hard case: one side lowers, the other throws
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what happens when neither side has easy access: one side must lower and the other must throw.
steps.simpleTranslation: If for one side it is by lowering and for the other by throwing, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the real question that the list of obvious cases was building up to. It is setting up a debate between רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The place is lower than one חצר and higher than the other, so neither side has easy access. The question is whether lowering counts as easier than throwing, or whether both are equally hard.

keyTerms.meaning: "What?" It opens a real legal question.

phrases.english: For this one by lowering and for that one by throwing, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the clear cases, it asks about the one case that is not clear.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who may use a place that one side reaches by lowering and the other by throwing?

steps.title: רב: both sides are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that neither side may use the place.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer. Neither side gets the place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, lowering and throwing are both hard ways to use a place, so neither side has an advantage. Both sides keep a share in it, and without an עירוב each side blocks the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Both are forbidden. Neither side may carry there.

phrases.english: Rav said: Both are forbidden.
phrases.notes: Each side's share blocks the other.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lowering and throwing are equally hard, so both sides are forbidden.

steps.title: שמואל: the place goes to the side that lowers
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says lowering is easier than throwing, and a place goes to whoever can use it more easily.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: We give it to the side that lowers. For that side, using it is easy, and for the other side it is hard. Anything that is easy for one side and hard for the other is given to the side for whom it is easy.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב. He gives the place to the side that reaches it by lowering, and he states a general rule to back this up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that lowering is easy compared with throwing. That makes this case just like the ones in step 13, where one side has the easier access. His general rule is that the easier user gets the place.

keyTerms.meaning: Its use: how that side uses the place.
Easily, comfortably.
With difficulty.
We give it, meaning we assign the place to that side.

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule "easy use beats hard use" is the key principle for deciding which side owns a shared space for carrying on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: נוֹתְנִין אוֹתוֹ לָזֶה שֶׁבְּשִׁלְשׁוּל.
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: We give it to the one who reaches it by lowering.
For this one, its use is easy,
and for that one, its use is difficult,
and anything whose use is easy for one side
phrases.notes: Here he states a general rule.

phrases.english: and difficult for the other,
we give it to the one for whom its use is easy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: נוֹתְנִין אוֹתוֹ לָזֶה שֶׁבְּשִׁלְשׁוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, opposing answer to the question that רב answered in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lowering counts as easy and throwing as hard, so the place goes to the side that lowers.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה of the balcony to test the debate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if the people of a חצר and of a מרפסת made no עירוב, anything ten טפחים high goes to the מרפסת and anything lower goes to the חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If the people of a חצר and the people of a מרפסת forgot and did not make an עירוב, anything ten טפחים high goes to the מרפסת, and anything lower goes to the חצר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings our משנה to try to decide between רב and שמואל. This step only quotes the source; the actual argument from it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An object ten טפחים high near a raised מרפסת is reached by the מרפסת people by lowering things onto it, and by the חצר people only by throwing. Yet the משנה gives it to the מרפסת, which looks like שמואל's view. The גמרא will now examine this.

keyTerms.meaning: "We learned" in a משנה. It introduces a quote from the משנה.
A raised balcony with stairs down to the חצר.
They made an עירוב, joining the properties so people may carry between them.

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not yet prove anything. It only quotes the משנה; the proof and any reply come in the next lines.

phrases.english: We learned: The people of a courtyard and the people of a balcony
phrases.notes: This is the משנה of our פרק.

phrases.english: who forgot and did not make an eiruv,
anything that is ten handbreadths high belongs to the balcony;
phrases.notes: The balcony people reach it by lowering.

phrases.english: less than this belongs to the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source from the משנה to decide the debate in steps 15-16.
steps.raayaObject: Deciding between רב (both forbidden) and שמואל (the side that lowers gets it).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה giving a ten-טפחים-high object to the מרפסת, which reaches it by lowering, rather than to the חצר, which would have to throw.

steps.title: What Does the Word 'Balcony' Mean Here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to explain the proof from the משנה. It first tells us what we might have assumed the word מרפסת means.
steps.simpleTranslation: It might have entered your mind to ask: what is the מרפסת mentioned in the משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא pauses to define the word מרפסת so we understand the משנה it just quoted. The actual definition comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from the משנה depends on how the people of the מרפסת reach the high spot. That depends on what a מרפסת actually is. The words קא סלקא דעתך tell us that what follows is a first assumption, not the final answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It might have entered your mind (introduces an assumption the גמרא will build on or test)
What is? (asks for a definition)
A balcony or raised walkway above a courtyard, with houses that open onto it

steps.confusionAlert: קא סלקא דעתך does not mean the גמרא is giving its final answer. It is showing how we might first understand the word before the proof is examined.

phrases.english: It might have entered your mind (to say):
phrases.notes: Signals a first assumption that the גמרא will work with or test.

phrases.english: What is (the meaning of) the balcony?
phrases.notes: Sets up the definition that will come next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the משנה quoted in step 17 as a proof, by first defining its key word מרפסת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the מרפסת in the משנה? This matters for knowing how its people reach the ten-טפחים spot, and whether that supports רב or שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: Continuing the proof from the משנה in step 17: the assumed meaning of מרפסת shows how its people reach the ten-טפחים spot, which bears on the debate between רב and שמואל.
